title: Marlowe Rewards Points Arithmetic for Reservation Fulfilment Orders
content:
This note gives the Marlowe Rewards calculation of the points credited by a missing-points adjustment on a reservation fulfilment order.

## Qualifying spend

The qualifying spend is the sum of the order's booked, cancelled and adjusted line amounts, after three deductions. Booking lines count as positive amounts. Cancellation, price-adjustment and late-promotion lines count as negative amounts.

- **Gift-card lines.** Deduct the amounts on any gift-card lines, whether e-gift card or plastic gift card.
- **Rewards Notes.** Deduct the amount captured on the order with Marlowe Rewards Notes.
- **Returns.** Deduct the merchandise already credited on returns of that order.

The result is never below zero and is kept to the cent.

## Points

The points equal the qualifying spend, multiplied by the base points per USD and by the points multiplier of the tier held on the handling date. The figure is rounded to the nearest whole point, a half point rounding up.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

**Example 1.**

| Order line or deduction | Amount |
|---|---|
| Booked apparel line | 140.00 |
| Booked footwear line | 60.00 |
| Booked e-gift card line | 25.00 |
| Price adjustment on the apparel line | minus 10.00 |
| Sum of line amounts | 215.00 |
| Less gift-card lines | 190.00 |
| Less 20.00 captured with Marlowe Rewards Notes | 170.00 |
| Less 30.00 merchandise credited on a return of the order | 140.00 |

With a base rate of 1 and a tier multiplier of 1.50, the points are 210.

**Example 2.** A qualifying spend of 33.33 with a base rate of 1 and a tier multiplier of 1.25 gives 41.6625, rounded to 42 points.

**Example 3.** Booked lines of 50.00, a Rewards Note capture of 20.00 and 45.00 credited on returns would give minus 15.00. The qualifying spend is held at 0.00, so the points are 0.
